title.purpose: Section headings and the quiz title in the context bar.

title-sm.purpose: Panel headings and the question prompt on Check.

body-lg.purpose: The lede under a page heading, max 62ch, ink-2.

body.purpose: Everything else; tabular figures, paragraphs max 70ch. Fields stay 16px so phones do not zoom.

label.purpose: Chips, pills, flags, register headings, hints.

mark.purpose: Figures inside marks and point totals in the answer margin. Pencil uses weight 400 in graphite.

score.purpose: The ringed total; 1.85rem in the large ring.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Floating things only: welcome register excerpt, class covers, toast, skip link, current question in the list, sheet tile on hover.

shadows.name: cover-hover
shadows.purpose: A class cover under a real pointer, with a 2px rise.

shadows.name: spine

shadows.purpose: Every keyboard-focusable element; fields use 2px with no offset.

motion.purpose: Pencil to pen: the red stroke draws over the pencil ghost; a second stroke starts 100ms later.

motion.name: ghost-fade
motion.purpose: The pencil ghost fades out under the new ink.

motion.name: ring-draw
motion.purpose: The score ring draws when a total settles.

motion.name: control

components.css: .ds-chip, .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 2px 9px; border-radius: 999px; font: 600 .8125rem/1.5 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Variable', 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', system-ui, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip-ink { background: var(--red-soft, #fbe9ec); color: var(--red, #c4122f); } .ds-chip-ink::before { content: ''; width: 14px; height: 2px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--red, #c4122f); } .ds-chip-pencil { background: var(--pencil-soft, #eceef3); color: var(--pencil, #5d6271); } .ds-chip-pencil::before { content: ''; width: 14px; border-top: 2px dashed var(--pencil, #5d6271); } .ds-pill { font-weight: 400; background: var(--device-soft, #dcf1ec); color: var(--device, #0a7563); } .ds-pill i { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; } .ds-flag { display: inline-flex; padding: 1px 8px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--hl, #ffdf3d); color: #1b1600; font: 700 .8125rem/1.5 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Variable', 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', system-ui, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; }

components.name: Marks

components.css: .ds-mk { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 28px; height: 28px; position: relative; isolation: isolate; } .ds-mk svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: visible; } .ds-mk path { fill: none; stroke-width: 2.6; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-ink path { stroke: var(--red, #c4122f); } .ds-pencil path { stroke: var(--pencil, #5d6271); stroke-width: 2.2; stroke-dasharray: 3 2.5; } .ds-needs::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 1px; border-radius: 4px; background: var(--hl, #ffdf3d); opacity: .55; z-index: -1; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-ink:hover path { stroke-dasharray: 1 2; stroke-dashoffset: 1.01; animation: ds-draw .25s cubic-bezier(.3, .7, .4, 1) forwards; } } @keyframes ds-draw { to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } }

components.description: A 38px register row: sticky name, ink and pencil cells, a red wash on a wrong cell, a pencil hatch on a waiting cell, the total behind a strong rule.

components.css: .ds-register { border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 0; background: var(--sheet, #ffffff); border: 1px solid var(--rule, #dfe5ef); border-radius: 10px; font: 400 .9375rem/1.5 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Variable', 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', system-ui, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; color: var(--ink, #17203a); } .ds-register th, .ds-register td { height: 38px; padding: 0 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #dfe5ef); } .ds-who { text-align: left; min-width: 140px; font-weight: 600; border-right: 1px solid var(--rule-2, #c5cfe0); } .ds-cell { min-width: 44px; text-align: center; transition: background-color .2s ease-out .15s; } .ds-wrong { background: var(--red-soft, #fbe9ec); } .ds-pending { background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, transparent 0 5px, var(--pencil-soft, #eceef3) 5px 7px); } .ds-register tr:hover td { background-color: var(--sheet-2, #eef2f8); } .ds-m { display: inline-block; width: 28px; height: 28px; } .ds-m svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: visible; } .ds-m path { fill: none; stroke-width: 2.6; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-mi path { stroke: var(--red, #c4122f); } .ds-mp path { stroke: var(--pencil, #5d6271); stroke-width: 2.2; stroke-dasharray: 3 2.5; } .ds-total { text-align: right; padding-right: 14px; border-left: 1px solid var(--rule-2, #c5cfe0); color: var(--red, #c4122f); font: 700 1.1rem/1 'Kalam', 'Segoe Print', cursive; }

narrative.overview:
Tickmark looks like the book a teacher keeps for a class: the class list down the left, the questions across, and a mark in every cell. A navy register cover (the top bar, primary buttons, the class covers on the welcome page) frames cool white paper. Everything on the paper is a working surface, not a dashboard: the register grid, panels ruled with hairlines, and one dominant work region per screen. The system turns down the SaaS dashboard of cards and KPI tiles. Results opens with one summary sentence and then the register itself.

The whole visual language exists to show **who made each mark**. Code and the teacher write in red ink, drawn as solid SVG strokes. Gemini Nano only suggests, so its marks are dashed graphite pencil. Highlighter yellow means "this needs you". Teal means "on this laptop" and slate means "in the cloud". Each of these colours carries one meaning and is not reused for decoration, so a teacher can read the state of a whole class at a glance. The tick, cross, half-tick, dash and question shapes, and hatching for "waiting", carry the same meaning without colour.

Density matches a real register: 38 px rows, tabular figures, sticky names and headings, and keyboard-first checking with one key per decision. The type is Atkinson Hyperlegible, chosen for legibility at night and for Indian-script fallbacks. The one hand-drawn voice is Kalam, and it is used only for the marks themselves. There is one authored motion: a pencil suggestion redrawn as a red-ink stroke when the teacher confirms it.
keyCharacteristics: Navy register cover over cool white paper; light ("Paper") and dark ("Chalkboard") themes from the same token names.
Every colour has a single meaning: red ink = decided mark, graphite = suggestion, yellow = needs you, teal = laptop, slate = cloud.
Status reads in greyscale: distinct mark shapes, solid vs dashed strokes, hatched cells for waiting.
Dense, ruled, flat surfaces; one shadow token for things that float.
Atkinson Hyperlegible for every label and number (tabular); Kalam only for marks and scores.
One signature motion: pencil to pen in 250 ms, skipped under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Red Ink Rule
rules.body: Red is a mark someone stands behind: a stroke, a ringed score, a point total, the margin rule, the "Ink" chip, or the button that inks a mark. It is never interface chrome. Tabs, the current question, delete buttons and confirmations are navy or grey.

rules.name: The Highlighter Means You Rule
rules.body: Yellow appears only where the teacher has to act. If nothing is waiting, there is no yellow on the screen.

rules.name: The Laptop-or-Cloud Rule
rules.body: Teal is on this laptop, slate is the cloud, and the two are never swapped or used decoratively. Where data went is the product's claim, so its colour must stay honest.

rules.name: The Hand Is For Marks Rule
rules.body: Kalam sets marks, scores and point totals only. Nano's reasons, question numbers, headings and labels stay in Atkinson; Nano's reason is Atkinson italic in graphite.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every figure on screen is tabular, so register columns, totals and counts align without extra work.

rules.name: The Flat Register Rule
rules.body: Working surfaces (panels, the register, answer rows) never take a shadow. Only things that float or are lifted for a pointer do, and touch screens drop hover lifts.

rules.name: The Shape Is Meaning Rule
rules.body: Tick, cross, half-tick, dash and question mark are distinct shapes, solid is decided and dashed is suggested, so the register reads correctly in greyscale and for colour-blind teachers.

dos: **Do** make the register (or a ruled list) the first thing on a working screen, with one dominant work region taking most of the width.
**Do** draw every new mark state as its own shape and stroke (solid for decided, dashed for suggested), so it reads in greyscale.
**Do** keep red for marks, scores, point totals, the margin rule, the "Ink" chip and the inking action only (the Red Ink Rule).
**Do** show yellow only where the teacher must act, and teal or slate only to say where data was processed.
**Do** use Atkinson Hyperlegible with tabular figures for every label and number, and Kalam only inside marks and scores.
**Do** keep working surfaces flat: sheet white, 1 px hairlines, 6 px controls, 10 px panels; use the Lift shadow only for floating things.
**Do** give every motion a reduced-motion path, and keep 44 px targets and hidden keyboard legends on coarse pointers.
**Do** define both themes from the same token names; never hard-code a light-only colour in a component.
donts: **Don't** build KPI tiles, stat-card rows or dashboard cards; put counts in a sentence or the register's foot row.
**Don't** use red for tabs, navigation markers, delete buttons, confirmations or decoration.
**Don't** set sentences, reasons, question numbers or headings in Kalam.
**Don't** credit cloud Gemini output to Gemini Nano, or colour a cloud reading teal.
**Don't** add uppercase eyebrows or kickers above headings; the context line goes after the heading.
**Don't** put shadows on panels, rows or the register, or lift on hover on touch screens.
**Don't** use text glyphs ("−", "+", "✓") as icons; use the drawn 24-unit, 1.8-stroke icon set.
